title: Numbered Markdown heading outline
instructions:
Build a numbered outline from a deliberately small Markdown subset.

## Files
- `outline.py`: implement `parse_heading` and `Outline`.

`parse_heading(line: str) -> tuple[int, str] | None` recognizes a heading
only with 0..3 leading ASCII spaces, 1..6 `#` characters, and then a space,
tab, or end of line. Strip surrounding whitespace from its text. Remove a
final run of `#` characters only if preceded by whitespace, then strip again.
For example `## Title ###` becomes (2, 'Title'), `# C#` keeps 'C#', and `#`
has empty text. Inline Markdown is preserved literally. No setext headings.
This helper does not track code fences.

`Outline()` starts empty. It has these public methods:
- `add(markdown: str) -> None`: scan `splitlines()` and append headings.
  Ignore headings inside fenced blocks. An opening fence has 0..3 leading
  ASCII spaces and a run of at least 3 backticks OR at least 3 tildes,
  followed by any text. Its closing fence must use the same character, a
  run at least as long, 0..3 leading spaces, and only whitespace after it.
  While inside a fence, everything except its matching closer is ignored.
  Unclosed fences hide the rest of this add call. Fence state starts outside
  at each add call, while numbering and entries persist across calls.
- `entries() -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]`: fresh list of (level, number,
  text) tuples. Numbering maintains six counters initially zero. A heading
  at level L increments counter L and resets all deeper counters to zero;
  its number joins counters 1..L with dots, with no final dot. Skipped
  levels remain zero: a first level-3 heading is '0.0.1'.
- `render() -> str`: entries joined by newline, each as `number + ' ' + text`,
  without indentation or final newline. Empty text retains that one space;
  an empty outline renders as ''.
- `reset() -> None`: clear entries and all counters.

All text arguments are strings; no validation of other types is required.
